paper_title: Detecting Ultralight Bosonic Dark Matter via Absorption in Superconductors
suggested_experiment_name: Aluminum superconductor dark matter absorption detector (1 kg-year exposure)
notes: This paper is a THEORETICAL PROPOSAL presenting sensitivity projections for a superconducting absorber detecting ultralight bosonic dark matter (meV–eV mass range). It discusses three distinct coupling types: (1) DarkPhoton (kinetic mixing κ, Fig. 3), (2) AxionElectron (pseudoscalar coupling g_ae, Fig. 4), and (3) ScalarElectron (scalar coupling d_φee, Fig. 5). The paper does NOT present a single measured exclusion limit; instead, it shows projected sensitivities for 1 kg-day and 1 kg-year exposures. Because the paper constrains MULTIPLE coupling types simultaneously and the primary contribution is methodological (demonstrating how superconductors can absorb ultralight DM via phonon emission), no single coupling_type can be assigned without ambiguity. The figures show sensitivity curves but do not provide explicit numerical (mass, coupling) pairs in tabular form. Extracting precise data points from the figures is unreliable due to resolution and the overlapping constraint curves. The DM density ρ_X = 0.3 GeV/cm³ is stated in Eq. (3) and applies to all three models. This is a haloscope-type experiment (direct detection of relic DM in the galactic halo), so dm_density_assumed is set. The paper's main value is conceptual/methodological rather than providing a definitive new exclusion limit that supersedes prior work across all three coupling types simultaneously. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Extracted lower boundary of exclusion region from FIG. 5 (Scalar dark matter plot). The y-axis label is d_sce, which represents the dimensionless scalar coupling to electron mass. The exclusion region is above the boundary curve. Sampling is denser at low masses (1-10 meV) where the boundary has steeper slope, and sparser at higher masses (100 meV - 1 eV) where the boundary flattens. The 1 kg-year curve (thicker line) provides the stronger constraint and was traced.
